label: Palestiniens tués (Gaza)
source: Gaza Ministry of Health / UN OCHA / WAFA / IMEMC (Sep 27, 2026)
contestNote: Israël conteste ces chiffres et soutient que des combattants du Hamas sont comptés comme des civils. Total cumulé depuis le 7 oct. 2023, dont plus de 21 500 enfants ; plus de 8 000 personnes toujours portées disparues sous les décombres dans toute la bande (certaines estimations : 4 000-5 000 ; environ 8 000 corps supplémentaires seraient ensevelis selon la défense civile de Gaza, 6 sept.). L'enquête de mortalité du Lancet (mars 2026) estime à 75 200 les décès violents jusqu'au 5 janv. 2025 — 34,7 % de plus que le ministère de la Santé pour la même période. Netanyahou a rejeté le 9 août 2026 la feuille de route en 15 points pour Gaza des États-Unis/du Conseil de la paix malgré l'acceptation du Hamas ; Israël affirme qu'il n'y aura aucun retrait de Tsahal tant que le Hamas ne sera pas véritablement désarmé. Une déclaration du Conseil de la paix du 12 août indique que le retrait de Tsahal au-delà de la Ligne jaune attend le démantèlement complet par le Hamas de ses armes légères/lourdes et de ses tunnels. Plus de 1 394 tués et plus de 4 839 blessés depuis l'entrée en vigueur du cessez-le-feu d'oct. 2025, dont 831 corps retirés des décombres (ministère de la Santé de Gaza via WAFA, 20 sept.) ; le porte-parole de l'ONU Stephane Dujarric a déclaré le 31 août que l'ONU reste « très préoccupée par l'impact sur les civils en raison des frappes aériennes israéliennes continues ». L'émissaire du Conseil de la paix Mladenov a averti le Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU le 26 août qu'un effondrement du cessez-le-feu serait un « point de non-retour pour tous ».
delta: Sep 25 (351st consecutive ceasefire-violation day): Israeli soldiers shoot and kill Rania Salama Saad in the al-Mawasi area of Rafah; Israeli forces shell a displaced-persons' tent in al-Sawarha, al-Zawayda, wounding several, while a drone fires two more missiles into the area and armored vehicles open heavy fire near Bureij; a separate bombardment of a vehicle near the American Hospital in al-Zawayda kills one unidentified Palestinian; five more wounded (one critically) near Haifa School, Khan Younis. Gaza Health Ministry's 24-hr toll: 5 killed, 35 wounded; ceasefire-period toll reaches 1,408 killed, 4,916 wounded (834 bodies recovered); cumulative toll reaches 73,928 killed, 175,030 wounded. Sep 24 (350th day): an Israeli drone strike kills Jaber Kamal Meqbel, 35, in northwestern Deir al-Balah, wounding 8; a second drone strike hits the vehicle carrying his body near al-Baydar, southwest of Gaza City, wounding 9 more; a drone strike on a group near the al-'Abdasawi Supermarket in Khan Younis wounds Hasan Takrim al-Battah, who later dies of his wounds; Israeli forces shoot and kill Muhannad Abu Medyin, 33, west of al-Zahra in central Gaza. Sep 23 (349th day): a joint IDF/Shin Bet strike on a vehicle in al-Mawasi, western Khan Younis, kills Muhammad Abu Alwan, whom Israel names Hamas' finance chief, and Osama Abu Khater; separate strikes kill one more each in Deir al-Balah and Gaza City; Israeli forces shoot and kill Yahia Sammour north of Khan Younis and fatally wound Noura Diab in the Bureij refugee camp; Al Jazeera puts the day's overall toll at 7 killed strip-wide; the US-backed Board of Peace unveils a $2.45B, 66-project Gaza reconstruction blueprint at the UN General Assembly, contingent on Hamas disarmament. Sep 22 (348th day): an Israeli drone strike near the Muscat school in al-Tuffah, Gaza City, kills two and wounds three amid at least eleven documented ceasefire violations that morning; separate shelling near al-Nafaq Street, east Gaza City, kills Adham Sobhi Ziyara and wounds three more. Sep 21 (347th consecutive ceasefire-violation day): Israeli tank fire on displaced-persons' tents in the al-Mawasi 'safe zone' west of Khan Younis kills 11-year-old Ismail al-Bardawil; an Israeli drone kills Mohsen Ahmed Bahjat in Jabalia; tank fire kills 31-year-old Fidaa Toutah on Salah al-Din Street east of Nuseirat as she returns from taking her children to school; a separate drone strike kills an unnamed man in Khan Younis city center hours later. Ceasefire-period toll reaches 1,394 killed, 4,839 wounded; cumulative toll reaches 73,914 killed. Sep 20 (346th consecutive ceasefire-violation day): IDF/Shin Bet disclose killing three Hamas operatives over the weekend — Yahya Hamdouna and Mohammad Rafa'i (both Daraj-Tuffah Battalion, Oct 7 participants) and Basir al-Barsh, whom the military names a Nukhba commander; the third matches Basir al-Bursh, son of Health Ministry chief Munir al-Bursh, whose family disputes the militant characterization. Two more wounded by gunfire near Khan Younis. Sep 19 (345th day): a drone strike kills Basir al-Bursh, 28, in Jabalia's az-Zahra neighborhood while he helps fill water containers; a separate drone strike on a vehicle in Sheikh Radwan, Gaza City, kills 24-year-old Mohammad Khaled al-Refa'ey and wounds 4+; a Shujaiya strike kills 1 more; a girl dies of Friday's gunfire wounds near Nuseirat. Ceasefire-period toll reaches 1,393 killed, 4,822 wounded; cumulative toll reaches 73,910 killed, 174,935 wounded. Sep 18 (344th consecutive ceasefire-violation day): Israeli soldiers shoot and kill Karam Mus'ad al-Masar'a on Julis Street in the Nuseirat refugee camp; two more Palestinians wounded near Nasser Medical Complex, west of Khan Younis, bringing to five the number wounded there since Thursday afternoon. Sep 17 (343rd day): Israeli drone strikes kill Youssef al-Zaim near the 17th Roundabout in western Gaza City and Mohammad Nasser Suleiman al-Bayouk in Nahr al-Bared, Khan Younis; a strike on Ad-Daraj School in central Gaza City wounds two, and a Sheikh Ajlin drone strike wounds around 10; Sa'id Barham dies of earlier strike wounds; IDF discloses killing Hamas Nukhba operative Muhammad Jamal Ahmad Eid (Bureij) and naval-force platoon commander Saleh Ziad Ibrahim Miqdad (Gaza City). Gaza Health Ministry reports 5 killed, 28 wounded strip-wide in 24 hrs; ceasefire-period toll reaches 1,386 killed, 4,784 wounded. Sep 16: A war-damaged six-storey building (Al-Saada) collapses overnight in western Gaza City, killing at least 21 (incl. 12 children) and wounding 14, with dozens still missing under the rubble; separately, an Israeli 'double-tap' drone strike in Sheikh Radwan, north Gaza City, wounds a Civil Defence paramedic then kills 15-year-old Mohammad Abdul Zinati as he goes to help him; IDF strikes overnight also kill a Hamas commander in northern Gaza and two more militants. Ceasefire-period toll reaches 1,381 killed, 4,757 wounded. Sep 15: IDF and Shin Bet say they killed Hamas Rafah Brigade commander Nael Abu Obeid in a southern Gaza Strip strike after weeks of tracking; separate strikes destroy four tents and kill two at the Abu Khadra displacement camp, central Gaza. Sep 14: IDF says it killed Hamas Jabaliya Battalion commander Ahmad Batash in northern Gaza overnight — at least the fifth Hamas commander eliminated that week; Gaza Health Ministry reports 2 more killed, 25 wounded strip-wide in 24 hrs, incl. 8 wounded (4 children) in Khan Younis tent strikes. Sep 13: Israeli drone strike on a vehicle in Tal al-Hawa, western Gaza City, kills two people IDF says were Hamas engineers, wounds 13; medics say the bodies were too dismembered to identify. Sep 12: Israeli drone strikes hit displaced Palestinians' tents in Al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis, including near the Shahd Rest Area; 4-9 wounded (reports vary), no fatalities. Sep 7: Israeli strikes kill 5 across Gaza in 24 hrs — a drone strike kills Mohammad Sukkar (28) in Rimal, Gaza City; a vehicle strike kills Yousef Aqila and his 7-year-old daughter Wafaa in western Gaza City as they returned from buying school supplies; an artillery strike on the Sakina School shelter in Deir al-Balah kills 7-year-old Saadi Ghalia; Hassan Ali Saqallah (19) also killed in Gaza City; 17 more wounded strip-wide. IDF separately discloses killing PIJ operative al-Batrihi in Shati camp (Sep 6) and Hamas Nukhba member Khalas in a prior strike, plus a mid-air munition diversion to avoid civilians. US envoy Kushner says Israel's government is acting 'a little irrational' on Gaza due to next month's election. Sep 6: Israeli strike kills 2, incl. a girl, in Al-Nasr, Gaza City; Gaza City holds a mass funeral for 100 people (incl. 60 children) recovered from Zeitoun rubble; 8 Muslim-majority nations warn of 'grave consequences' over Katz/Ben Gvir Gaza-displacement proposals; Netanyahu says he 'attacked Qatar' and defends Qatari aid-fund transfers to Gaza. Sep 5: rescue teams recover remains of 55 Malka family members from Zeitoun rubble; a new Freedom Flotilla mission sets sail toward Gaza, expected in October; US Ambassador Huckabee denies any Israeli plan to forcibly displace Gazans. Sep 4: US State Department publicly rejects Israeli displacement plans, citing Point 12 of Trump's peace plan guaranteeing no forced departure from Gaza. Sep 3: Israeli drone strike on Rimal kills a 13-year-old; IDF shoots dead two Palestinians crossing the Yellow Line near Beit Lahia; National Security Minister Ben Gvir unveils 'Disengagement 710,' a plan to remove 1.86 million Palestinians from Gaza over seven years. Sep 2: Gaza Health Ministry reports 8 killed, 31 wounded in 24 hrs (cumulative toll 73,470+); Israeli drone strike and gunfire kill 2 more in Jabalia town/refugee camp, hitting displacement tents and a civilian gathering; ceasefire-period toll reaches 1,334 killed, 4,429 wounded. Defense Minister Katz says Israel is 'organised and prepared' to remove Gaza's population 'by any means' once Trump approves, calling the plan merely 'frozen'; Netanyahu visits an IDF post in Gaza and says Israel will not withdraw from territory it controls. Sep 1: Shin Bet commandos raid the Al Katiba area of western Gaza City, capturing wounded Hamas internal security chief Muein al-Arabid; IAF strikes cover the operation, killing at least 3 (incl. al-Arabid's wife) and wounding 8; separately, Israeli strikes elsewhere in Gaza kill at least 4 more including children. Aug 31: Israeli drone strikes kill 5 in Gaza City — 2 near the municipal park (residential building entrance, displaced-family area) and 3 in a vehicle strike in Tal al-Hawa; IDF says both hit Ezzedine al-Qassam Brigades operatives. Ceasefire-period toll reaches 1,318 killed, 4,375 wounded. Aug 30: IDF says it killed Nukhba company commander Hani Abd al-Hai Fakhri Mazloum and sniper Hassan Zidan Hassan Deiri in northern Gaza; a separate Deir al-Balah strike kills Hamas operative Hassam Osama Hussein Nasir and 3-year-old Tayyem Hamdan. Aug 29: Israeli strikes kill at least 6 more Palestinians — 2 in a Gaza City drone strike on an electric bike, 1 in Khan Younis, 1 by gunfire in al-Musaddar village, plus 2 more Nukhba Force members (Yasser Abu al-Khair, Mohammed al-Din) killed in a separate Khan Younis strike and Nukhba cmdr Abd al-Fatah Abu al-Eish (Oct 7 participant) and operative Raed Adel Mohammed Alyan killed in Jabalia; a drone strike hits a medical-supply tent inside the Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital compound in Deir al-Balah for the second time in a month, wounding 3; Gaza Health Ministry reports 10 bodies received in 48 hrs, ceasefire-period toll reaches 1,313 killed, 4,361 wounded. Aug 28: Israeli strikes kill 5 in Gaza — 3 from the Abdeen family in a drone strike north of Khan Younis, Hassan al-Deiri in a Sabra (Gaza City) drone missile strike, and 1 more in a Mashahra tent strike; IDF claims (without evidence) it killed Hamas operative Qais Bitawi and two Hamas/PIJ commanders. Aug 27: Israeli strikes kill 3 more Palestinians — a tent near Shati camp west of Gaza City (IDF says it killed Hamas anti-tank cmdr Bilal Raqi'i), a drone strike on a displacement tent in al-Mawasi, Khan Younis (IDF says it killed Hamas Khan Younis Brigade member Azzam Abadala), and a drone strike on an electric bicycle at the Al-Sinaa intersection in Gaza City; Defense Minister Katz renews threat to evacuate Gaza areas over kite launches. Aug 26: Palestinian Health Ministry reports 7 killed in 24 hrs (5 new, 2 died of earlier wounds), plus separate drone strikes kill 1 more in a Khan Younis displacement tent and 1 more near the Ansar junction west of Gaza City; ceasefire-period toll reaches 1,303 killed, 4,336 wounded; Board of Peace envoy Mladenov warns UN Security Council of a ceasefire 'point of no return.' Aug 25: Israeli strikes kill 7 — 3 in a Beit Lahiya home strike near Kamal Adwan Hospital, 1 in an al-Mawasi (Khan Younis) drone strike, 3 from earlier wounds; a warehouse holding child-nutrition aid destroyed; Israel expels Dutch reps from the Kiryat Gat Gaza coordination center over a Dutch settlement-goods import ban. Aug 24: Strikes hit a mosque and desalination plant in Gaza City's Sheikh Radwan area and destroy the historic Abu Salim Mosque in Deir al-Balah (IDF says it targeted Hamas weapons storage); a Bureij refugee camp strike kills 4-year-old Hassan al-Hafi; separately IDF strikes kill 2 Hamas militants in Deir al-Balah, one an Oct 7 Nukhba fighter. Aug 23: Netanyahu and Katz threaten to 'intensify strikes' over kites landing near Nahal Oz; IAF strikes kill Hamas weapons-production cmdr Abu Ful in Maghazi and a 4-year-old boy in Az-Zawayda near an aid site; Khan Younis shelled along the Yellow Line; Israel raises concerns about Hamas disarmament provisions in deal framework.

label: Palestiniens blessés (Gaza)
source: Gaza Ministry of Health / UNRWA / WAFA / IMEMC (Sep 25, 2026)
contestNote: 22-25 sept. : 35 blessés dans l'ensemble de la bande le 25 sept. selon le ministère de la Santé de Gaza, dont 5 près de l'école Haïfa, à Khan Younès, et plusieurs lors du bombardement de la tente d'al-Zawayda ; 9 blessés dans les frappes de drone du 24 sept. à Deir al-Balah/al-Baydar, 4 à 5 autres lors de la frappe sur le supermarché de Khan Younès ; plusieurs blessés lors des frappes des 22-23 sept. à Tuffah/al-Nafaq/Khan Younès/Deir al-Balah/ville de Gaza. Les chiffres peuvent être sous-estimés en raison d'un système de santé débordé ; plus de 4 839 blessés depuis le seul cessez-le-feu d'octobre 2025. 21 sept. : 9 blessés transportés depuis Khan Younès et Bureij en lien avec les meurtres d'al-Mawasi, Jabalia, Nuseirat et Khan Younès. 19-20 sept. : plus de 4 blessés dans la frappe sur un véhicule à Sheikh Radwan/rue Ar-Rashid (dont 2 enfants), 1 de plus près de Maghazi, 21 blessés dans toute la bande en 24 h jusqu'au 20 sept. 17-18 sept. : plus de 28 blessés dans toute la bande, dont la frappe de drone de Sheikh Ajlin (~10), la frappe sur l'école Ad-Daraj (2) et d'autres blessés près du complexe médical Nasser, à Khan Younès. 17 blessés le 7 sept. dans toute la bande en 24 h, dont 6 lors de la frappe de drone à Rimal, 6 lors de la frappe sur un véhicule dans l'ouest de la ville de Gaza, et d'autres près de Bureij, Nuseirat et Khan Younès. 31 blessés le 2 sept. dans toute la bande en 24 h, dont plusieurs lors de la frappe de drone/des tirs à Jabalia ; 8 blessés le 1er sept. lors du raid du Shin Bet et des frappes de couverture de l'IAF à Al Katiba, ville de Gaza. Plusieurs blessés le 31 août lors de la frappe de drone sur le parc municipal de la ville de Gaza ; blessures légères également signalées le 31 août à la suite de tirs d'une vedette israélienne sur des pêcheurs au large de la ville de Gaza, de tirs/éclats à Khan Younès, et d'une femme grièvement blessée à Deir al-Balah. Plusieurs autres blessés le 29 août lors de la frappe de drone sur l'entrepôt de l'hôpital des Martyrs d'Al-Aqsa (3) et lors de la frappe du 30 août à Deir al-Balah.

Structures détruites/endommagées à Gaza
contestNote: Fin 2024, on estimait que 60 % de l'ensemble des structures étaient endommagées ou détruites

label: Camions d'aide entrant à Gaza (moyenne quotidienne)
contestNote: Les entrées d'aide ont reculé de 37 % du 11 janv. au 11 avr. par rapport aux trois premiers mois du cessez-le-feu : moins de 105 000 tonnes métriques contre 167 600 tonnes métriques requises. Environ 102 à 122 camions/jour entraient à la mi-avril contre plus de 600 nécessaires. Le point de passage de Zikim a rouvert le 12 avr. un jour sur deux ; Kerem Shalom (Karem Abu Salem) est le principal point de passage actif ; Kissufim reste fermé. Route Jordanie B2B : 60 camions deux fois par semaine. Respect des quotas de carburant à 14 %. L'appel d'urgence 2026 demande 4,1 Md$, financé à seulement 9,7 %. Environ 129 cuisines communautaires servent 1,25 M de repas/jour. Le bureau de presse du gouvernement de Gaza a indiqué le 6 août 2026 que seulement environ 35 % des camions d'aide attendus sont entrés à Gaza depuis le cessez-le-feu d'oct. 2025, ainsi que 4 091 violations documentées du cessez-le-feu en 300 jours.

label: Établissements de santé endommagés/détruits
contestNote: Les 36 hôpitaux de Gaza endommagés ou détruits ; ~16 partiellement fonctionnels au plus fort. Le directeur général du ministère de la Santé de Gaza, le Dr Munir al-Bursh, a averti le 25 août 2026 que seules 12 des 34 stations d'oxygène restent opérationnelles et que seuls 4 des 30 dispositifs de remplissage de bouteilles fonctionnent encore, ce qui menace les unités de soins intensifs, néonatals et pédiatriques.

label: Population menacée par la phase 5 de l'IPC (catastrophe)
contestNote: Israël conteste la qualification de famine. Justin Brady, de l'OCHA, a indiqué qu'environ 10 % de la population de Gaza est désormais au bord de la famine (août 2026) ; le risque persistant de famine demeure malgré une certaine amélioration depuis la confirmation de la famine dans le gouvernorat de Gaza en août 2025. Les familles survivent généralement avec un seul repas pauvre sur le plan nutritionnel par jour ; certaines passent des journées entières sans manger, recourant au rationnement, à l'emprunt et à la récupération. L'accès à l'aide reste limité par le pillage et la distribution militarisée. L'appel urgent 2026 demande 4,1 Md$ pour 3,6 M de personnes à Gaza et en Cisjordanie ; il reste gravement sous-financé.
